item.title: Empowering School Engagement: The Hidden Role of “Enablers” in Science Communication - ENJOI - Science communication
item.description: A JCOM study highlights the key role of “enablers” in involving school students in science. Through programs like Darwin Day and Plastic Pirates, enablers bridge research and education by aligning goals, translating visions, applying theory, and evaluating engagement outcomes

item.title: Empowering Curiosity in a Science Center: A Conversation with Miha Kos - ENJOI - Science communication
item.description: Miha Kos, a physicist, is the director of Slovenia’s first hands-on science centre, Hiša eksperimentov (founded 1996 in Ljubljana). He’s been there since its start and says his dreams came true.

item.title: Mapping how the world talks about science - ENJOI - Science communication
item.description: A global survey reveals how 72,000 people in 68 countries encounter and discuss science — and why understanding these differences matters for engagement and democracy.

item.title: Excellence and Innovation in Science Journalism: A Conversation with Michele Catanzaro - ENJOI - Science communication
item.description: Michele Catanzaro is a lecturer at the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (Spain), where he teaches science and health journalism, and an award-winning freelance journalist who contributes to outlets such as El Periódico, Nature, Science, and others. He coordinated the PerCientEx project on excellence in science journalism and was part of the ENJOI European project. item.title: Science in School: Make it fun, make it matter - ENJOI - Science communication
item.description: PISA 2022 shows declining STEM and literacy skills in Europe, especially among disadvantaged students. Science in School helps address this by offering free, engaging resources that connect science to real life and support teachers in boosting student curiosity.

item.title: Trends and challenges in science: A philosophy of science perspective - ENJOI - Science communication
item.description: The Science Lens report examines future trends and challenges in science, highlighting fragile research ecosystems, geopolitics, AI risks to democracy, and the growing role of science communication.

item.title: Pure Objectivity in Science is a Myth. And has consequences for Science Communication - ENJOI - Science communication
item.description: Science isn’t as neutral as it claims to be. Sara Giordano argues that research is shaped by cultural values and power, and that acknowledging this can strengthen trust and communication. She calls for a more democratic science—grounded in evidence, but responsive to the communities it affects.

item.title: Social media at the core of science magazines — what the Science case tells us - ENJOI - Science communication
item.description: Social media are becoming increasingly central to the survival and relevance of magazines and news outlets. They are no longer just channels for promoting published stories, but key spaces where editorial identities are negotiated, audiences are built, and engagement is measured in real time. item.title: When press releases become public science communication - ENJOI - Science communication
item.description: Science News Agencies increasingly reach the public directly. A new study proposes an index to assess whether their press releases are transparent, accessible, and socially relevant—highlighting how improving these texts can strengthen public engagement with science.
